newsitem.title: USA: N. Dakota senator blasts Canadian wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: N. Dakota senator blasts Canadian wheat imports.

text.p: North Dakota durum and barley producers have lost nearly $270 million during the past three years because of Canadian imports, North Dakota Sen. Byron Dorgan said on Monday.

A study by North Dakota State University showed that Canadian imports have reduced durum wheat prices by an average of 6.4 percent during the past three years, and lowered barley prices by an average of 5.8 percent during the same period, Dorgan said in a statement.
Dorgan, who commissioned the study, said he sent the results to U.S. Trade Ambassador Charlene Barshefsky, who is currently involved in trade talks with Canada.

"North Dakota is the largest producer of both durum and barley in the nation and has suffered the brunt of the impact of these price reductions," Dorgan said in the statement. "The evidence continues to mount that this unfair agreement has hit North Dakota farmers squarely in the pocketbook in a big way."
Wheat producers in the state have pressed for the U.S. government to slow Canadian imports.
Last week, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he was concerned about the impact of Canadian wheat and was monitoring the imports closely.

Canadian and U.S. officials have previously projected wheat and barley shipments to U.S. buyers would be about 1.4 million to 1.5 million tonnes in the year ending Sept. 12. That level would be roughly equal to a trade ceiling established in 1994 but which has since lapsed.
